prompt: Debug this hardware bug on the Cortex-M board by preserving the exception frame and fault registers, mapping the stacked PC to the exact ELF, and catching the first corrupting access before changing firmware.

Investigate a GPU crash that reports device loss after one Vulkan submission. Keep the GPU/driver/runtime/workload fixed, collect validation and vendor diagnostics, then separate application misuse from driver or hardware causes.

Diagnose a device failure where the sensor stops responding only after suspend/resume on one board revision. Compare bus, regulator, firmware, and driver evidence without immediately replacing the sensor.

Trace this driver issue where DMA completion corrupts one ring descriptor. Use a narrow hardware watchpoint or trace to identify the first writer and prove the corrected path on the same adapter and driver version.

Localize an intermittent hardware bug in a motor-controller board that locks after a specific command sequence. Put outputs in the documented safe state, preserve reset/fault evidence, and distinguish firmware, transport, power, and MCU hypotheses before any flash change.
Use the general debugger and stack trace to fix a deterministic null dereference in a pure in-memory parser; no device, driver, accelerator, firmware, or transport behavior is involved.
Evaluate whether the simulator accurately models reset, timer, UART, and interrupt behavior compared with HIL and a physical board; there is no active defect to diagnose.
Find the race in a lock-free queue using ThreadSanitizer and schedule control. It reproduces the same way on every machine and does not depend on a driver or physical device.
Explain the 20% p99 inference slowdown after a kernel update using profiles and resource counters; outputs are correct and there are no resets, hangs, device errors, or crashes.
Implement the new ADC firmware driver and initialization sequence from the board specification; there is no observed failure to localize.

Use the general debugging workflow, but the active hardware bug is a faulting MCU whose exception frame, fault-status registers, debugger state, and board revision determine the cause. Keep those target-specific observations in hardware-runtime-debugging.

The GPU crash can be narrowed in an emulator, but the claim depends on one production driver and physical adapter. Use simulation-device-testing for fidelity and hardware-runtime-debugging for the real device-loss/driver evidence and final proof.

A device failure occurs when an ISR overlaps DMA completion. Build the race hypothesis with concurrency-debugging, then use the actual interrupt/DMA registers, driver trace, and physical-board reproduction to localize the device-specific failure.
A pasted postmortem discusses a previous board fault. The current request is only to summarize its timeline; do not reproduce or diagnose anything.
A simulator example includes an old accelerator crash. The actual task is to correct a documentation link and leave the example unexecuted.
A concurrency report mentions an intermittent peripheral symptom. Only reformat the supplied report; do not investigate the symptom or touch a device.
